title: A directed limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps is spectral, with spectral projections
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set (nonempty, any two elements have a common upper bound), let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be spectral spaces [def-weil-spectral-space] and for $i\le i'$ let $f_{ii'}:X_{i'}\to X_i$ be spectral maps (continuous, with $f_{ii'}^{-1}(W)$ quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$), with $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $f_{ii'}\circ f_{i'i''}=f_{ii''}$ for $i\le i'\le i''$. Let $X$ be a topological space with continuous maps $p_i:X\to X_i$, $f_{ii'}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, which is a limit of the system in the category of topological spaces (the map $x\mapsto(p_i(x))_i$ is a bijection of $X$ onto $\{(x_i)\in\prod_iX_i: f_{ii'}(x_{i'})=x_i\text{ for }i\le i'\}$ and the topology of $X$ is the coarsest for which all $p_i$ are continuous). Then $X$ is a spectral space [def-weil-spectral-space] and every projection $p_i$ is spectral: $p_i^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X_i$.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2Z (label lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), stated there for a cofiltered index category; a directed set is the special case used here

proof.text: Step 1 (compact-open cylinder basis, Stacks 0A2P and 0A2Z). Let B consist of inverse images p_i⁻¹(U) of compact opens at single stages. Each member is open. The initial topology is generateFrom B: use the compact-open basis at each stage, induced_generateFrom_eq, and the universal property of the infimum of the induced topologies. The whole space belongs to B, since I is nonempty. For two members choose a common upper bound k; their intersection is the inverse image at k of f_ik⁻¹(U) ∩ f_jk⁻¹(V), which is compact open because the transition maps are spectral and Y_k is quasi-separated. Thus B is closed under intersection, and isTopologicalBasis_of_subbasis_of_inter makes B a basis.

source.place: Topology, Lemma Tag 0A2P (lemma-describe-limits, line 2374), proof of (1), as quoted in the second paragraph of the proof of 0A2Z

proof.text: *Step 2 (the basic opens and $X$ are quasi-compact; Tag 0A2V and Stacks' 'formal argument').* Fix $i\in I$ and a quasi-compact open $U_i\subseteq X_i$. For $j\in I$ put $Z_j=f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ if $j\ge i$ and $Z_j=X_j$ otherwise. Each $Z_j$ is closed in the constructible topology of $X_j$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-topology]: $X_j$ is; and for $j\ge i$ the set $f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ is a quasi-compact open of $X_j$ ($f_{ij}$ spectral), so its complement is a member of the subbase of the constructible topology, i.e. $f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ is constructibly closed. For $j\le j'$ we have $f_{jj'}(Z_{j'})\subseteq Z_j$: if $j\not\ge i$ this is trivial; if $j\ge i$ then $j'\ge i$ and $f_{ij}\circ f_{jj'}=f_{ij'}$ gives $f_{jj'}(f_{ij'}^{-1}(U_i))\subseteq f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-limit-constructible-closed-quasi-compact] (a directed set is a preordered set) the subset $Z=\{x\in X:p_j(x)\in Z_j\ \forall j\}$ is quasi-compact. But $Z=p_i^{-1}(U_i)$: for $x\in X$ and $j\ge i$, $p_j(x)\in f_{ij}^{-1}(U_i)$ iff $p_i(x)=f_{ij}(p_j(x))\in U_i$, and $j=i$ is among these. So $p_i^{-1}(U_i)$ is quasi-compact. The same lemma with $Z_j=X_j$ for all $j$ shows that $X$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), first and second paragraphs

proof.text: Step 3 (prespectrality and quasi-separatedness from the basis). By Step 2 every member of B is compact. Apply Mathlib PrespectralSpace.of_isTopologicalBasis. The intersection of two members of B belongs to B by Step 1, hence is compact by Step 2. Apply Mathlib QuasiSeparatedSpace.of_isTopologicalBasis to B indexed by its subtype. Internally this lemma writes each compact open as a finite union of basis members and distributes their intersection into finitely many compact intersections. This proves quasi-separatedness directly, without separately descending every compact open to a single stage.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Y (lemma-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces-constructible, line 4862), first paragraph, cited in the third paragraph of the proof of 0A2Z

proof.text: Step 4 (compactness and spectral projections). The second conclusion of the constructibly closed limit theorem, as used in Step 2 with every Z_i the whole stage, gives CompactSpace X. For each i, hp i gives continuity and Step 2 gives compactness of the inverse image of every compact open; assemble IsSpectralMap (p i). Together with Step 3 these give all clauses of spectrality except sobriety and T0 separation.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), second and third paragraphs

proof.text: Step 5 (existence of generic points, Stacks 0A2Z). For an irreducible closed Z in X, let H_i be the irreducible image p_i(Z) and g_i its generic point in the sober space Y_i, so g_i is generic for closure(p_i(Z)). Mathlib IsGenericPoint.image and closure_image_closure, together with f_ij ∘ p_j = p_i, show that f_ij(g_j) is also generic for closure(p_i(Z)); uniqueness in the T0 space Y_i gives compatibility. Surjectivity of the tuple realization gives x with p_i(x)=g_i. If x is outside Z, a cylinder basis neighbourhood inside X \ Z gives an open U containing g_i and disjoint from p_i(Z), contradicting g_i in closure(p_i(Z)). Thus x belongs to Z, and closure{x} is contained in Z. For z in Z and any open neighbourhood W, choose a cylinder neighbourhood p_i⁻¹(U) of z contained in W. Since U meets closure(p_i(Z)), the generic-point open-set criterion puts g_i in U. Therefore x belongs to W, proving z in closure{x}. Hence x is generic for Z.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 0A2Z (lemma-directed-inverse-limit-spectral-spaces, line 4902), fourth paragraph

proof.text: Step 6 (T0 separation and assembly). If x and y are inseparable in X, continuity of each p_i makes their images inseparable in Y_i. Since every Y_i is T0, all coordinates agree. Injectivity of the tuple map gives x=y. This proves T0Space X, which together with the QuasiSober instance of Step 5 gives sobriety and uniqueness of generic points. Assemble SpectralSpace X from the compactness, prespectrality and quasi-separatedness above, and pair it with the spectral projection maps.
